title: Record the review of phase 7: five findings, fixed
message:
Record the review of phase 7: five findings, fixed

The plan's phase 7 record gains the review of MR !26: the five findings,
the two commits that fix them and what was found on the same code, the
consequences decided with the fix, the tests, and the verification on
dd9732777. Work item #31 is filed for the mail letters that take rnum 1.

title: Keep what a live object made its own across an OLC save
message:
Keep what a live object made its own across an OLC save

An OLC save wrote the new prototype over every live object of it and
kept only the object's place in the world. Random treasure and crafted
gear are live objects of a carrier prototype rewritten field by field,
so a save of a carrier, for any change, gave every generated weapon or
armour in the game the carrier's blank stats, and the next player or
house save made the loss permanent. The same save took a player's
restring, arcane mark and scribed spellbook pages, a disenchanted
essence's level and a resized item's size and dice.

update_all_objects() now leaves the object in place and gives it, field
by field, the new prototype's definition where the object still held
the old prototype's, and keeps what it has of its own: what a reload
from a save would also have kept. Strings it shared with the old
prototype become the new one's, an extra description list of its own
that ends in the old prototype's now ends in the new one's, and an
ability list, spellbook or restring identifier that still matched the
old prototype becomes a copy of the new one's. add_object() keeps the
old prototype until the live objects are done and frees its strings
after them.

The same save and the editor copies had three more faults, found in
review:

- The overwrite dropped the object's script while it stayed registered
  for random and time triggers, with any waiting trigger still
  scheduled, so the save loop's extract_script() never ran. Once the
  object was extracted, the next random dispatch or the resumed wait
  read the freed object. The script is runtime state of the object: an
  OLC save no longer touches it, and overwrite_object() keeps the
  target's, which also ends a preview copy sharing the script of the
  object it previews.
- overwrite_object() kept a live target's hash links but took the
  source's rnum, so a preview copy of another prototype's object stayed
  on the carrier's chain under the other rnum, and an iedit commit after
  a new prototype moved the rnums wrote the edit copy's old rnum onto the
  live object. A live target now keeps its rnum.
- A container's weight counts what it holds, and so does its carrier's.
  The overwrite replaced the weight in place, so a save or an iedit
  commit left the totals off by the change, and a container that lost
  its contents' weight went negative when they were taken out. Both
  paths now give the object its own weight plus what it holds, by the
  capacity it has now, and carry the change to its holders as
  obj_to_obj() counts them.

Found while fixing: add_object() lost the old prototype's trigger list,
which oedit_save_internally() means to free, and each live object's
trigger list. Both are freed now.

Tests in test_gameplay_e2e.c, each failing on the code before the
change and clean under valgrind:

- Test_gameplay_object_prototype_save_keeps_what_each_object_made_its_own
- Test_gameplay_object_overwrite_keeps_weight_totals
- Test_gameplay_object_prototype_save_extracts_live_scripts, through
  oedit_setup_existing() and oedit_save_internally()
- Test_gameplay_object_copy_keeps_a_live_targets_rnum

Test_gameplay_object_prototype_save_leaves_live_objects_whole now checks
that the restrung and marked object keeps its name and mark. The suite
has 2049 tests, so MAX_TEST_CASES rises from 2048 to 4096.

Review findings on MR !26.

title: Move renumbered objects to the hash chain of their new rnum
message:
Move renumbered objects to the hash chain of their new rnum

A new prototype below others renumbers their live objects up in
adjust_objects(), and delete_object() renumbers them down. obj_rnum_hash
is keyed by the rnum, but both left every object in the bucket of its old
one: get_obj_num() missed it, and extracting one that headed its old
bucket set the new bucket's head to its successor, dropped that chain, and
left the freed object at the head of the old bucket for the next
read_object() there to write into. Each renumbered object now leaves its
chain and joins the chain of its new rnum.

Found on the same two loops:

- delete_object() renumbered objects with no prototype too. NOTHING is the
  largest rnum, so a corpse or a pile of coins took a bogus rnum that
  extract_obj() then used as an obj_index subscript. Both loops now skip
  NOTHING, and so does the renumbering of the notice boards, where an
  insert turned a board with no object into rnum 0.
- A mail letter or a forged note gets rnum 1 from create_obj() without
  joining a chain (work item #31). Removing it from the hash emptied the
  bucket of whatever chain was there, and the renumber loops now remove
  every object they move. remove_obj_from_rnum_hash() leaves a chain the
  object does not head alone.
- delete_object() never freed the deleted prototype's strings and trigger
  list. Its spellbook and abilities are still given up, not freed: an edit
  copy can point at them.

Test_gameplay_object_renumber_keeps_the_hash_and_unnumbered_objects
inserts a prototype below two others and deletes it again, with an
object of no prototype, a letter and a board with no object beside them.
It ends in a segmentation fault before the change, fails without the
chain check in remove_obj_from_rnum_hash(), and is clean under valgrind.
Review finding on MR !26.

title: Keep a live object's own links and lists when another object is written over it
message:
Keep a live object's own links and lists when another object is written over it

Two functions wrote one whole object over another and then put back a
list of the target's runtime fields: update_all_objects(), for every
live object of a prototype that OLC saves, and copy_object_main(), for
the editor copies. Each list was older than fields the struct has
gained.

After an OLC save of a prototype, each live object of it

- pointed at the prototype's special abilities and spellbook, which
  free_obj() frees with the object: extracting one live object freed the
  prototype's lists under it and under the other live objects;
- had lost its hash links while still on its obj_rnum_hash chain, and
  its sheath pointers, trap, group-loot link and pending limb slot;
- had dropped its own strings, arcane mark and restring identifier
  without freeing them.

The iedit commit wrote back the hash links, sheath pointers and trap the
object had when the edit began. An edit copy shared a corpse's
description of the fallen with the live object, and both freed it.

overwrite_object() is now the one place that says what the target keeps:
where it is, what holds it and what it holds, its list, hash and
registry links, its events and transfer state, and what only the
running game gave it. copy_object_main() and update_all_objects() both
go through it, and the iedit commit no longer restores a list of its
own.

For an OLC save, each live object frees its strings before the
prototype's are replaced, while they can still be told apart, and gets
copies of its own of what read_object() copies: give_obj_own_copies() is
that part of read_object(). copy_object_strings() duplicates the
description of the fallen. index_object() clears the slot a new
prototype goes into, since the copy keeps the target's runtime fields;
oedit_setup_existing() clears its edit copy for the same reason.

Left as it was: the special abilities and spellbook a live object held
before the save are dropped without a free. A preview copy and an open
edit copy can point at the same lists (work item #29), so freeing them
here could free one list twice.

Tests: an OLC save with two live objects of the prototype, an editor
copy and commit across a change of the live object's links, and a new
prototype in a slot full of stale data. The second ends in a double
free before the change; the other two fail.

Work item #30.
